about: The one description of Deedglass (VIRAL-3 PRD-04). docs/description_test.go checks README.md, AGENTS.md, server.json, context7.json, npm/deedglass/package.json (description and keywords), the Claude Code plugin and marketplace, the Docker catalog entry, internal/installlinks.Description (the Claude Desktop bundle and the Goose link), the docs home page's description and the docs site's llms.txt (docs-site/astro.config.mjs reads this file) against it, and the network sentence word for word in README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/LICENSING.md and the docs site's licences page. `github` is the GitHub repository description (at most 350 characters; set it with `gh repo edit deedglass/deedglass --description`, after the PR that changes it merges); its first sentence is the README's heading. `short` is the tagline cut to fit Cursor's 80-character tagline (integrations/cursor/listing.json). The slogan 'See what your agents actually did.' (the CLI banner, email footers, the docs home heading) is a slogan, not a description, and stays as it is; the docs home <title> is 'Deedglass Docs' because the tagline is longer than a 60-character title. Change the wording here first, then in each file. Plain names per docs/NAMING.md. Claims: P-325 (github; it rests on P-060, P-089, P-134, P-086), P-097 (tagline, summary; it rests on P-057, P-060, P-069), P-086 (licence), P-104 (network; it rests on P-087 and P-052).
tagline: Deedglass: rules decide each AI agent tool call; it checks what really changed and seals a record.
short: Deedglass: rules decide each AI agent tool call; it checks what really changed.
github: Check what your AI agents actually changed. Deedglass sits between agents and Postgres, FHIR servers, SaaS APIs and MCP tools: rules decide each call, a check after it compares what really changed with what the agent reported, each action is sealed as a signed record anyone can check offline, and Postgres rows can be undone. Apache-2.0 core.
summary: Deedglass sits between AI agents and the systems they change. Rules decide each tool call, a check compares what the system really changed with what the agent reported (Claimed, Checked or Proven; Matches, Doesn't match or Can't check), and each result is sealed as a signed record anyone can check offline. It can undo the rows an action changed.
licence: The core, the SDKs and the CLI are Apache-2.0. The features in `ee/` are FSL-1.1-ALv2 (free to use while we grow), and each release of them becomes Apache-2.0 two years after it ships. The release binary, the `@deedglass/cli-*` npm packages and the container image include `ee/`, so their licence is `Apache-2.0 AND FSL-1.1-ALv2`.
network: Every feature is free while we grow, so nothing checks a licence and nothing is sent to deedglass.com: the scan reads files on your machine and, with `--postgres-dsn-env`, connects only to the database you name. The `deedglass licence` commands, kept for a later paid option, are the only ones that call Dodo Payments or deedglass.com, and only when you run them; `DEEDGLASS_NO_NETWORK=1` stops those calls. `deedglass version --check` and the `--latest` option of `deedglass policy install` and `policy packs` contact GitHub when you use them. Head timestamps are off by default; with TSAs or a transparency service listed in deedglass.yaml, `deedglass deeds timestamp` and each export contact only those.
